text.p: These are the leading stories in Zambia's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Two policemen manning a road block in northern Zambia were shot dead by bandits on Tuesday, police said.
- President Frederick Chiluba warned his new cabinet that he would not hestitate to sack inefficient ministers and called for discipline among government officials.
- The central bank has decentralised the sale of treasury bills and government bonds, which will now be sold through commercial banks.
- More evidence that the ruling Movement for Multi-party Democracy rigged the November 18 general elections through double voting has surfaced.

- The Zambia Association of Manuafactuers has predicted more fuel price hikes in the near future to cover up Zambia National Oil Company losses during a shortage two months ago. Fuel prices were on Monday hiked by 15 percent.
